newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian assembly calls for new prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian assembly calls for new prime minister.

text.p: The president of Cambodia's National Assembly on Monday called for Foreign Minister Ung Huot to be approved as first prime minister in place of overthrown Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
The call came despite an announcement by Ranariddh on Sunday that Ung Huot was being temporarily expelled from his royalist FUNCINPEC party.
National Assembly president Chea Sim in his opening statement called on members to approve Ung Huot's nomination.
Ung Huot was named to replace Ranariddh by FUNCINPEC members who stayed in Cambodia after Ranariddh's overthrow on July 6.
There were 97 of the assembly's 120 members present for the Monday session.
"The FUNCINPEC party has now submitted to the National Assembly the candidacy of a marvellous FUNCINPEC prime minister," Chea Sim said.

"I now move to ask our august national assembly to examine this very important candidacy and provide its high decision and its vote of confidence in the continuation of the coalition leadership," he said.
Second Prime Minster Hun Sen, who ousted Ranariddh and has backed Ung Huot's nomination for the prince's job, was present at the session.
There was heavy security around the central Phnom Penh assembly building.

Assembly officials and parliamentarians said they did not expect the assembly to vote on Ung Huot's candidacy immediately as the paperwork needed to put it on the formal agenda had not been completed.
"It could be at least a week," said one official.
After overthrowing Ranariddh, Hun Sen said he wanted to keep the structure of the coalition government, formed after 1993 elections, in place.
FUNCINPEC won the 1993 poll with 58 of the assembly's 120 seats. Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party won 51 seats.

But Ranariddh agreed to a power-sharing coalition after Hun Sen, the leader of Cambodia's former Hanoi-backed government which ruled through the 1980s, objected to the poll result and the country faced division along factional lines.
Ranariddh, who left Cambodia before he was ousted, said in a statement released on Sunday that as president of the FUNCINPEC party, he was temporarily expelling Ung Huot from the party.
Ung Huot later said the prince's expulsion of him was an act of desperation.
"This is something like a joke ... this is a sign of desperation," Ung Huot told reporters late on Sunday.
"He cannot just sack anyone while he's running away like this," Ung Huot said. "It doesn't mean anything, I don't take it seriously."
Many Ranariddh loyalists fled the country after the prince's overthrow and more than 40 were killed, human rights workers say.
The party members remaining in Phnom Penh said they would work with Hun Sen as a coalition partner in the run-up to a general election in May.
